text.content: Stepping back: why is it the case that orgs have a relative few fulltime employees? What makes it hard for a single org to stretch to encompass more humans? I’ll go through four major historical drivers, and how AI might change each.

rich_text.plain_text: Stepping back: why is it the case that orgs have a relative few fulltime employees? What makes it hard for a single org to stretch to encompass more humans? I’ll go through four major historical drivers, and how AI might change each.

text.content: First, it’s hard to hire and onboard.

rich_text.plain_text: First, it’s hard to hire and onboard.

text.content: Hiring requires a lot of trust. An org wants to know that a person is a good fit, worth paying for. The job market is famously a market for lemons. Orgs try to vet candidates, but resumes are low-signal; interviews cost precious staff time, and also select for people good at interviewing. Ideally you would see the person doing the job — in a work test or work trial.

rich_text.plain_text: Hiring requires a lot of trust. An org wants to know that a person is a good fit, worth paying for. The job market is famously a market for lemons. Orgs try to vet candidates, but resumes are low-signal; interviews cost precious staff time, and also select for people good at interviewing. Ideally you would see the person doing the job — in a work test or work trial.

text.content: AI can change this by making search and matching problems much more efficient. And this is not just “pair up existing resumes & job listings”. AI can form a much more detailed model of a human based on all their public outputs, and a role’s requirements based on all of its outputs. Or: have your Claude apply for jobs, have their Claude interview your Claude to see if the fit is good.

text.content: Second, larger teams incur higher communication costs.

rich_text.plain_text: Second, larger teams incur higher communication costs.

text.content: The number of pairwise relationships grows quadratically with team size; Dunbar famously pointed to a cap of ~150 people per stable community. Startup literature preaches the gospel of small nimble teams.

text.content: Prosaic technology (Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, Zoom) is already enabling much larger & profitable orgs. AI can improve on this in several ways: connecting data sources smoothly (eg MCP); making it easier to spin up custom software to serve internal use cases, and (speculatively) by simulating other humans, letting one speak with a colleague’s digital twin.

text.content: Third, on-the-job learning historically leads to specialization.

rich_text.plain_text: Third, on-the-job learning historically leads to specialization.

text.content: As an employee continues in an org, they build up skills and tacit knowledge that are hard to replace, sometimes unique to their particular role. You’ll notice that great orgs work hard at staff retention. However, this kind of specialization is a double-edge sword for the employee. While it helps with job security, it also means that tenured employees accrue all kinds of responsibilities which hold back new work.

text.content: As more work is intermediated via LLM, LLM systems can hopefully take on more of specialization, first via in-context learning, then building up memory to reinforce particular skillsets. Humans today are still better at generalizing from few-shot examples, so their comparative advantage may remain as generalists, attacking new domains.

text.content: Paying for staff compensation is a major check on the growth of orgs. Successful orgs today draw an economic boundary around a few extremely great people, and pay them handsomely in cash and equity.

text.content: But in the long run AIs will drive down the cost of human upkeep. Surplus and abundance driven by rapid technical growth means that human consumption needs can be met much more easily. When people no longer rely on a paycheck to cover needs, they can spend their time with orgs which help fulfill their higher values.

Enshittification or shortform videos or gambling addictions or doomy content sucking out unendorsed hours from its prey. And, at the extreme end, xrisk: frontier lab employees endangering the rest of humanity.
